clue.text: Instrument made of stone, and lined with wood

indicators.note: the abbreviation for stone has the timber word laid along its inside, as a lining sits within

parts.note: ST is the standard abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight
pine is a familiar kind of wood

explanation.surface: Someone describes a musical instrument built from stone with a wooden lining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lined with' puts PINE inside ST; 'made of' is only a link. A stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds, abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A small harpsichord-like keyboard of the 18th century is a kind of musical instrument.

clue.text: Number supporting school punishment vocally

parts.note: someone supporting a cause is pro it

indicators.note: vocally says the word for the punishment is to be spoken, giving letters that sound the same

parts.note: the cane was a traditional British school punishment

explanation.surface: A complaint that a figure is being used to back up corporal punishment in schools, said out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a figure but something that numbs: a local anaesthetic. 'vocally' turns CANE into its sound-alike CAINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A local anaesthetic deadens feeling, so it is literally a numb-er, a thing that numbs.

clue.text: Recently appointed employee who'll make sweeping changes?

definitions.text: Recently appointed employee who'll make sweeping changes?

parts.words: Recently appointed employee who'll make sweeping changes?
parts.note: an idiom for a newcomer eager to reform, read literally as a fresh brush that will do some sweeping

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says a freshly bought brush sweeps clean, so a newcomer in post is expected to overhaul things.

clue.text: If bitten by dog one sets off alarm

indicators.note: the word if is held in the dog's jaws, so it sits inside the breed name

parts.note: a terrier is a breed of dog
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that if a dog bites you, someone will raise the alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one sets off alarm' reads as a burglar alarm, but it means someone who frightens; the dog does the biting in the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Something or someone that frightens people is one who causes alarm.

clue.text: Rushed round front of large farm building down under

indicators.note: the word for rushed goes round the next letter, enclosing it

parts.note: to woosh is to move with a rushing sound, so rushed can be wooshed

indicators.note: front of means take the first letter of large

explanation.surface: Someone hurried around a large barn somewhere in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts L, the first letter of 'large', inside WOOSHED. 'Down under' means Australia or New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia and New Zealand the shed where sheep are shorn and fleeces baled is a farm building.

clue.text: Give advice in vain, as he treats new ASBO skittishly

indicators.note: something done skittishly is done in a jumpy, unpredictable way, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice is given in vain as a man responds to a new antisocial behaviour order frivolously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link; 'skittishly' rearranges HE TREATS NEW ASBO. An ASBO was a British antisocial behaviour order, a court order restricting nuisance conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak to no effect, with counsel nobody heeds, is the idiom of using up air for nothing.

clue.text: Shoot, though not now, Mr Capone

parts.note: something done later is not done now
Al Capone was the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A command to fire, but not yet, addressed to the gangster Al Capone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' looks like a verb aimed at a gangster, but it is the botanical noun.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany a side shoot growing from a main stem is called a lateral.

clue.text: Military equipment used in intense conflict over Egyptian capital

indicators.note: in a down clue the war sits over, above, the following letter

parts.note: hard can mean intense, as in hard frost
a war is a conflict

indicators.note: capital means the first letter of Egyptian

explanation.surface: Weapons used in a fierce war over the city of Cairo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like Cairo, but it is the first letter of 'Egyptian', E.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardware is a common term for military weaponry such as tanks, guns and aircraft.

clue.text: Prudent individual, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for individual is spoken, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: discrete means separate or individual

explanation.surface: A single careful person, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example', but it signals the sound-alike: DISCRETE said aloud gives DISCREET.
explanation.definitionFit: Being careful in speech and conduct, avoiding giving offence, is a synonym of prudent.

clue.text: In favour of fighting extremely dangerous attackers

parts.note: to be for something is to be in favour of it
war is fighting

indicators.note: extremely means the outermost letters of dangerous

explanation.surface: Supporting a battle involving very dangerous assailants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like a booster for 'dangerous', but it takes that word's first and last letters, D and S.
explanation.definitionFit: In football and rugby the attacking players are called forwards.

clue.text: Intergalactic travel's earliest origins?

parts.note: beginnings in general, playfully pictured as the first steps of a journey between the stars

explanation.walkthrough: A container in spirit: T, the earliest letter of 'travel's', sits among STARS, so it is intergalactic. 'Intergalactic' would be both STARS and the container signal, so it is shown as a cryptic definition of 'origins'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beginnings or origins are what one makes when setting off; the word hides the heavenly bodies of space travel.

clue.text: Fine few words from a hippy musical

indicators.note: a line from a show is placed after the show's name

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical about hippies
a line is a few words, as from a script

explanation.surface: A decent short quotation from a counterculture stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like a verdict on the quotation but means very thin, as in a fracture; 'from' orders the pieces as a line from the show.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack or margin so thin it is like a single strand from the head is called very fine.

clue.text: Piece of furniture kept back from prewar days

indicators.note: kept back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An antique table or chest saved from the years before the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' marks the hidden run REWARD in 'prewar days'; 'kept back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sliding storage box in a chest or desk is itself loosely called a piece of furniture.

clue.text: Specifically, book smuggled into exam could be Chinese

indicators.note: the letters for specifically and the book are sneaked inside the exam word

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam
i.e. (id est, that is) introduces a specific restatement
NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A student caught sneaking a book into an exam; it might be Chinese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' is a link showing the definition is by example; 'smuggled into' signals the container. NT, the New Testament, counts as one book here.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental is an old-fashioned adjective for things from East Asia, so Chinese things are an example.

clue.text: One shot off to produce article on Tripoli's trouble

indicators.note: in a down clue the article sits on top of the rest

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so the letters of Tripoli's are disturbed

parts.note: the city name with its s, taken as letters

explanation.surface: A gunshot fired to cause unrest in the Libyan capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges TRIPOLIS (the 's counts) into IRPISTOL, under A.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistol firing pellets by compressed gas is a weapon that one fires, something shot off.

clue.text: Name such as Hilary

definitions.meaning: a word used to name a thing, as in a technical expression
Hilary is the name of the spring session at Oxford University and the Inns of Court

explanation.definitionFit: A word for something is its name; the academic year divides into sessions such as Hilary.

clue.text: Court official upsets Welshman

parts.note: to tip something over is to upset it
Taff is a slang name for a Welshman, from the River Taff

explanation.surface: A court officer knocks over a man from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: TAFF is British slang for a Welshman, after the river through Cardiff.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff is a sheriff's officer or bailiff in a court, originally carrying a metal-tipped staff.

clue.text: The old country (so I heard) is devastated

indicators.note: something devastated is wrecked and its parts scattered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An émigré has had word that the homeland has been laid waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so I heard' looks like a hearsay aside, even a sound-alike signal, but it is the fodder; 'is' is a link. The OCR dropped the D of 'heard'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodesia was the former name of Zimbabwe, a nation that no longer exists under that name.

clue.text: Lift lid off crime

indicators.note: the lid is the top, so the first letter is removed from the crime word

parts.note: theft is a crime

explanation.surface: Raise the cover after a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lid off' drops the first letter, T, from THEFT.
explanation.definitionFit: To heft something is to lift it, often to gauge its weight.

clue.text: Perhaps what wearer of designer label has for the figure

parts.note: a hep person is stylish, the sort who wears designer clothes
a tag is a label
to have clothes on is to wear them, so has becomes on

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what a fashion victim has stitched in, offered as a shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one picture: a HEP (dated slang for fashionable) person has a TAG ON. 'Perhaps what' and 'for the' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A seven-sided polygon is a plane geometric figure.

clue.text: Aristocrat almost penetrates barrier roundabout girl

indicators.note: the shortened peer goes into the barrier word

parts.note: a fence is a barrier

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the aristocrat word is dropped

parts.note: a lord is an aristocrat

explanation.surface: A noble breaks through a fence near a traffic roundabout, girl in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts LORD to LOR; 'penetrates' puts it in FENCE. Florence is the girl in The Magic Roundabout, a classic British children's TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence is the young girl character in The Magic Roundabout, so she is a girl of that show.

clue.text: Keep book on piano

indicators.note: the book word is placed on, after, the piano letter

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: Leave the book lying on the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' and 'piano' look like objects, but are verbs and a musical abbreviation; 'on' puts RESERVE after P.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve something is to keep it safe or keep it from decay.

clue.text: Deception to hold up old man as saint

indicators.note: in a down clue the trick sits below and holds up the father word

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
a trick is a deception

explanation.surface: A con is pulled to delay an elderly man posing as a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold up' looks like a robbery, but in a down clue TRICK is under PA, supporting it.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Patrick is the patron saint of Ireland.

clue.text: Rather dull night out in Kent

parts.note: Kent is in the SE, south-east, of England
a date is a night out together

explanation.surface: An evening out in Kent was something of a bore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. Kent is a county in south-east England, SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate means calm and unhurried, which shades into staid or somewhat dull.

clue.text: Parties? Leave plans to host one

indicators.note: the plans word hosts, holding inside it, the numeral

parts.note: rosters set out who is on duty and who is on leave
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A party question, and a decision to leave the plans for one guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parties' is a verb: to party is to make merry noisily. 'to host' puts I inside ROSTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to celebrate boisterously, so someone who roisters is partying.

clue.text: A publication briefly circulated by English inhabitant of Brisbane

indicators.note: circulated means the shortened word is turned around
briefly means the last letter of the publication word is cut

parts.note: an issue of a magazine is a publication

explanation.surface: A magazine is handed round by an Englishman to someone living in Brisbane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts ISSUE to ISSU; 'circulated' reverses it to USSI. Brisbane is a city in Queensland, Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Aussie is the informal word for an Australian, and Brisbane residents are Australians.

clue.text: Unfortunately, no agent will accept a single Greek play

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take in, accept, the single letter
unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one, a single

explanation.surface: Sadly an agent refuses even one Greek drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' rearranges the two words into ANTGONE; 'will accept' signals the single letter going inside. Antigone is by Sophocles.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigone is a tragedy by Sophocles, a classic of Greek drama.

clue.text: German language is pretty straightforward?

parts.note: frank means candid or straightforward
pretty means fairly, like the suffix ish meaning somewhat

explanation.surface: A remark that the German tongue is fairly simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link. Frankish was the West Germanic speech of the Franks.
explanation.definitionFit: Frankish was the Germanic tongue of the Franks, an ancestor of Dutch, so broadly a German language.

clue.text: Tree in hideaway by lake

parts.note: taken as written
a den is a hideaway or lair

explanation.surface: A tree stands inside a retreat beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but supplies its letters; 'by' joins L to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The linden is the lime tree, its common name in Europe and America.
